intended_object: The bijection Hom_{O_X}(M ⊗ N, P) ≃ Hom_{presheaves}(M ⊗ᵖʳᵉ N, P), i.e. the sheafification adjunction applied to the presheaf tensor product of two O_X-modules. Inferred from the docstring and from the `tensorHomEquiv_apply` lemmas that follow it.
explanation: This is not a mathematical object in its own right. It is an API device: Mathlib's `PresheafOfModules.sheafificationHomEquiv` (the hom-equivalence of the sheafification adjunction) applied to the identity morphism of the structure sheaf and to the presheaf tensor product `M.val ⊗ N.val`. The docstring says so itself: the point is to state the universal property "with the exact presheaf-morphism codomain of `sheafificationHomEquiv`", so that later proofs can rewrite with it. That codomain includes the `restrictScalars (𝟙 _)` wrapper. Mathematically it encodes the universal property of the sheafified tensor product (sheaf maps M ⊗ N → P correspond to presheaf maps out of the pointwise tensor product). The body matches that universal property and has no error, since `tensor M N` is presumably defined as the sheafification of `M.val ⊗ N.val`. Still, as a definition it is a bookkeeping bijection used for proofs, not a new notion.
